subject: A guideline for measuring animal traits for NicheMapR?

messages.author: ad331caa97d1c9b0
messages.subject: A guideline for measuring animal traits for NicheMapR?
parts:
Hi Mike,

Is there a guideline for measuring animal traits that could be used in NicheMapR? For example, how to measure "fur depth/density" for mammals and "feather length" for birds? These measurements seem simple but may not have been conducted for most of the species.


Best,

Liang

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: A guideline for measuring animal traits for NicheMapR?
parts:
Hi Liang,

Not that I know of but over the next three years I have funding to put together a trait database for mechanistic modelling which will also involve definition of protocols for measurement.

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: a05ad4db1ef329a2
messages.subject: Re: A guideline for measuring animal traits for NicheMapR?
parts:
Hey Mike,

Just to tag on to this conversation, do you have the protocol established yet and/or any way to contribute to the database?  I am primarily interested in salamanders (which honestly seem a bit more complicated in terms of mechanistic modeling) and will be collecting physiology data in the future.  Much of the current work was unfortunately delayed due to COVID-19, but it would be great to standardize future measurements.  I am still unsure how well NicheMapR will work for the salamander species I am working with, especially since I think many of the thermal traits are tied to humidity/VPD, where Tpref, VTmax, etc. would likely vary depending on VPD conditions.  However, with that said it would still be great to contribute to a database with standardized procedures (even if using other modeling approaches).
